diagnosis.root_cause: R84 paused source-owned shader HUD took a uniform pause scale in the original WVP path, but the sibling physical XYZRHW ESC path applied game-presentation-to-XR-eye pixel aspect containment. At 3440x1440 versus 2496x2688, this lets the same pause menu element families carry different vertical optical dimensions.
diagnosis.original_evidence: HEAD 127b5614 R30HudContainScale applied sourceOverTarget optical containment to XYZRHW while R30BuildScreenSpaceEyeConstants' exactPauseShaderOwner kept hudScale._11 and ._22 at userScale. The dispatch difference is statically verifiable; no physical HMD assertion made.
source_trace: Original ESC game state and pause exact arrow producer enter R30IsPauseMenuElement and select source-owned ScreenHud.
R30HudContainScale derives sourceOverTarget from the presentation frame and coherent pair of XR eye extents for native physical primitives.
R30 original-WVP shader branch now borrows that exact owner-sensitive containing scale only for exact pause-owned shader arrows before reconstructing the existing bilateral world-locked HUD plane.
The native and shader paths retain the existing per-eye FOV, vertical shift, pose generation and original 2D/non-ESC fallback.
alternatives_rejected: Enlarging every HUD/WVP shader, globally changing OpenXR eye FOV, or re-enabling older ResponsiveMenuScale would affect previously protected HUD and double-enlarge Quest pause controls.
diagnosis.eye_ownership: Source +TIME/GOAL and generic HUD never opt in. Only the two R84 ESC eye submissions of an exact paused ScreenHud source reuse common native pixel scaling while preserving their independent eye pose and projection.
